messages:
anika: quick question — noticed high tail latency on /v1/embeddings when clients send very sparse vectors (most dims 0). prefetch is batching them into large windows and we end up with big GPU wakeups + poor KV cache reuse. thinking of a lightweight 'sparse_prefetch_throttle' that: detect <=X non-zero dims, cap prefetch concurrency, or route to a small-batch pool. thoughts?

mike: can you paste an example request payload?

anika: sure
```json
{"model":"redwood-embed-v1","inputs":[{"id":"a","vec":[0,0,0,0.123,0,0,0.032,0,...]},{"id":"b","vec":[0,0.001,0,0,0,...]}]}
```

jess: ugh yeah — seen similar traces. cache hit rate collapses because shapes look identical but semantics differ (sparse vs dense). what if we expose a `prefetch_hint` in preflight so clients can opt-in ('sparse'|'dense') and the console surfaces a mismatch warning?

rahul: i don't love requiring client changes. keep server-side heuristic first, feature-flag the opt-in header, and roll behind console toggle. also we need telemetry: `sparse_prefetch_rate`, `prefetched_bytes_p90`, `sparse_tail_latency_ms_p99` per-customer.

anika: agreed. proposed plan:
1) server detection: nonzero_count / length < 0.05 => mark sparse (fast sample first 64 dims)
2) optional header `X-Embed-Prefetch-Hint: sparse|dense` for client opt-in
3) routing: cap prefetch concurrency for sparse and route to small-batch pool when available
4) console toggle: Routing -> Embeddings -> Prefetch heuristics (off by default for rollout)
5) add telemetry + per-customer breakdown + alert when sparse-prefetch causes >5% tail latency regression

olga: product note — in the console show a tiny banner: "Traffic appears sparse — enable sparse-prefetch protection to reduce latency & cost." CTA: enable for this project (with brief explainer).

mike: implementation note: avoid scanning entire vector on hot path. use a probabilistic sample of first N dims then extrapolate. emit `sparse_detect_sampled` event (sampled) so we can measure correctness without full scan overhead.

jess: also need to think quotas — prefetch still counts toward byte budget. if we route sparse to small-batch pool, adjust soft quota thresholds or have explicit bypass budget so projects aren't unexpectedly throttled.

rahul: +1. add a safe fallback behavior: if small-batch pool is saturated, fallback to dense pipeline but with shorter timeouts and an early circuit-breaker metric so we can revert quickly.

deploy-bot: canary: started rollout of prefetch-heuristic featureflag `emb.prefetch_heuristic_v1` to 5% customers in us-east-1 at 2026-03-20T14:12:00Z

anika: i'll write a short RFC + console mock and include the telemetry/alert thresholds. who can pair on the heuristic impl? @mike?

mike: i can take server side + sampling telemetry. jess can own quota integration & SLO checks.

olga: i'll do the copy and console CTA mock.

anika: thanks — i'll drop a short tech spec in #eng-docs and link back here. keeping this behind a toggle seems safest for rollout.
